§11.1.1 Cover Every Data Point

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

charts-cover-every-data-point · charts basics

✅ Normative

A chart MUST be rendered as a chart table that holds every data point the chart draws: every category position × every series, plus every printed callout that belongs to a position. A data point MUST NOT be skipped because it is hard to read; it MAY be left out only when no printed text can locate it or it is genuinely unreadable.

A chart is a data display, so its conforming rendering is its content — see Images and Figures§12.1.2. A rendering that gets a few prominent points right while the rest of the chart is missing is not a rendering of the chart.

What full coverage means

Chart Data points the chart table MUST hold
Grouped or stacked bars positions × series (the sample below: 6 years × 4 groups = 24 values)
Single series one per position
Printed callouts and totals one each, where a printed label can locate them — see Legend and Overlay Values§11.2.4
Multi-panel figure every panel, without exception — see Multiple Charts and Reference Ink§11.1.3

Two kinds of position MUST still be covered:

  • A labeled position with no mark is a data point whose value is 0 — the histogram's empty 1500 bin is 0 (see Bars and Histograms§11.2.1).
  • A position the axis does not label is located by its axis value: 2023 on a year axis that ticks every third year, 2500 on a bin axis that labels every other bin. The printed, regularly labeled axis is the calibration; a position that no printed calibration reaches is not locatable.

What may be left out

The default is in. A data point that can be read MAY be left out only when:

  • no printed text can uniquely locate it — see Labels§11.1.2; the unnamed companion curve in Legend and Overlay Values§11.2.4 is the standing example; or
  • it is genuinely unreadable — too blurred, too dense, or overlapping beyond judgment.

Leaving a point out MUST NOT be replaced by invented text: a made-up series name, a made-up category or a placeholder cell stands for nothing on the page (see Never Drop, Never Invent§2.2).

The page is the only reference

Values are read from the page. A value MUST NOT be shaded towards what some parser or earlier rendering produced, and a correct value stays correct however many renderings disagree with it (see The Page Is the Ground Truth§2.1).

The chart table

Every table representing a chart MUST open with <table data-source="chart">. The data-source="chart" attribute belongs on the opening <table> tag, including when the chart prints a data grid that supplies the table's content (see Chart With a Printed Data Grid§9.1.2). A table representing an ordinary printed table MUST NOT carry data-source="chart".

The layout of the chart table. A chart table MUST be laid out as follows, so that every chart table reads the same way — category down, series across:

  • one HTML <table data-source="chart"> per chart or panel, at the chart's place in reading order;
  • the chart's title, subtitle or caption in <caption> inside that table, first or last according to reading order (see Titles Banners Captions§9.7.3); its printed notes and source follow the table;
  • one row per category position (axis tick, bar, bin, slice, tile, region, named point), in the order the axis runs — left to right, top to bottom, a pie clockwise from the top;
  • a first column holding the category labels, then one column per series in legend order;
  • a header row holding the printed series names, its first cell holding the printed category-axis title or left empty; a single series with no printed name is headed by the printed value-axis title; when nothing printed names any column, the table has no header row;
  • a printed total that is not itself a category (a stack total above its bar) sits in a last column under an empty header cell;
  • printed text of the chart that is not a data point — axis titles not used as headers, unit notes, reference-line labels, event callouts, annotation boxes, legend entries of series that carry no value — follows the table as plain text in reading order.

The value in each cell is governed by Values and Tolerances§11.1.4; the labels in the first column and the header row by Labels§11.1.2.

✅ Sample — digital-services-survey-2024_p62

Six stacked bars over six labeled years, four legend series, every segment printing its value: full coverage is 6 × 4 = 24 values, all printed, so all copied as printed — count and share together.
